### Phase 0: Diagnostic — Week -1 (Non-Negotiable Before Any Plan)

Take one full official practice test for EvAU / Selectividad under **real conditions**: timed, same delivery (paper/computer/centre/online), correct tools (calculator policy per EvAU / Selectividad), real breaks, no pauses, no lookups.

**Record on one page:**

| Metric | Your Score | Target | Gap | Notes |
|--------|------------|--------|-----|-------|
| Total / Composite / Overall | | | | Percentile? |
| Section 1 | | | | Weakest domain — priority 1 |
| Section 2 | | | | Weakest domain — priority 2 |
| Section 3/4 if applicable | | | | |
| Timing left / rushed / guessed | | | | Pacing fix needed? |
| Delivery comfort (paper vs computer) | | | | Decide before Week 1 |

**Error log (spreadsheet — mandatory from Day 1):** Date | Section | Q# | Domain | Format (MCQ/TITA/NAT/WR) | Error Type (Content / Careless / Timing / Strategy) | Root Cause | Fix Action | Retest Date

**Categorise every miss for EvAU / Selectividad:**
- Content: Did not know formula / definition / rule
- Careless: Misread operator (NOT/EXCEPT), unit, selected wrong variable, darkening error
- Timing: Spent >2x average and still wrong → skip candidate
- Strategy: Did not use allowed aid (Desmos/calculator/highlight/whiteboard) or misapplied

**Decision point after diagnostic for EvAU / Selectividad:**
- Within 10% of target → Weeks 1-2 = advanced tactics + pacing refinement (not content)
- 20-30% below → Weeks 1-2 = content mastery on weakest 3 domains (official question bank, easiest → hardest)
- >30% below → Extend foundation to 6 weeks before heavy simulation; add 2 weeks to calendar

For EvAU / Selectividad, the diagnostic also reveals delivery fit — do all subsequent practice in the delivery you will sit.

### Weeks 1-2: Foundation — Close Content Gaps (The Highest-ROI Weeks)

**Goal:** 80%+ on official question banks for weakest 3 domains/subjects for EvAU / Selectividad.

| Activity | Hours | Method for EvAU / Selectividad |
|----------|-------|---------------------|
| Weak Domain Practice | 6 | Official question bank: easiest -> hardest, untimed then timed; tag each with domain |
| Diagnostic Review | 3 | Deep-dive every wrong answer: write why correct is correct + why your choice is wrong |
| Content Review | 2 | Official syllabus/bulletin for EvAU / Selectividad — not coaching summaries or social media |
| Mini-Timed Sets | 1 | 10-15 questions mixed domains, 70% of full time — build discrimination |

**Domain priority for EvAU / Selectividad (University Entrance):**
- If verbal/reading/listening is weak: argument structure, inference, T/F/NG vs Y/N/NG distinction, vocabulary in context, note-taking for audio-once
- If quantitative is weak: arithmetic foundations (percent, ratio, averages, time-speed, time-work), algebra, data interpretation, geometry/trigonometry (formula-dependent)
- If writing/integrated is weak: task achievement (overview, position, bullet coverage), cohesion (paragraphing, linking, reference), citation of evidence vs opinion
- If data/science/professional judgment is weak: graph extraction in 15 seconds, variable/control identification, ethics application

**Vocabulary / Formula / Mechanism system (where applicable for EvAU / Selectividad):** Start spaced repetition Day 1 (Anki/Quizlet) — 20 new/day + daily review. For EvAU / Selectividad this may be words, formulas, organic mechanisms, or statutes depending on domain; the system matters more than the list. 5 min review at morning/evening.

**Deliverable end of Week 2:** Complete official practice sets for weakest 3 domains at 80%+. Re-take diagnostic Section 1(s) — target 75%+. If not, repeat Week 2 — do not proceed; foundation is the base for EvAU / Selectividad.

### Weeks 3-4: Integrated Practice & Pacing Control (From Silos to Paper)

**Goal:** Seamless transitions between domains; section timing under control with buffer.

| Activity | Hours | For EvAU / Selectividad |
|----------|-------|-------------|
| Full Section Practice (timed, with checkpoints) | 4 | 1 full section x 2 per week, timed, same delivery |
| Official Practice Test 2 (Week 4 weekend, full sim) | 3 | Full paper/CBT, same time of day, same calculator/aid, real break, no pauses |
| Error Log Review (categorize every miss) | 3 | Monday + Friday review: pivot = careless vs timing vs strategy |
| Weak Domain Maintenance (30 min x 4 weak topics) | 2 | Targeted official items only |

**Pacing checkpoints (adapt to EvAU / Selectividad's timing — Fase General (4-5 obligatorias) + Fase Especifica (hasta 4 optativas), 90m per examen):**
- Example: Q9 at 10 min, Q18 at 20 min per module where module = 30-35 min
- Flag uncertainty in 10 seconds; return only if buffer remains (5 min left)
- No penalty for guessing where applicable for EvAU / Selectividad — never leave blank; multiple-darkening = wrong for OMR

**Week 4 Deliverable:** Practice Test 2 under full conditions. Compare to diagnostic: +5 to +15% (or +0.5 band / +10-20 scaled points) expected. If Section 1 performance still gates access to higher difficulty (where EvAU / Selectividad is adaptive) or sectional cutoffs still failing, extend foundation 1 week before proceeding. That gating is the single most leveraged fix for EvAU / Selectividad.

### Weeks 5-8: Hard-Section Mastery, Tool Fluency & Full-Paper Stamina

**Goal:** Dominate hard items; tool use automatic in <60 seconds; stamina for EvAU / Selectividad's full duration.

| Activity | Hours | For EvAU / Selectividad |
|----------|-------|-------------|
| Official Practice Tests 3 & 4 (adaptive if applicable) | 6 | Full papers, scored, with percentile |
| Hard-question sets (top 25% difficulty, official source) | 4 | Filter official bank by hard flag; time per item |
| Tool/Calculator/Annotation/OMR drills | 2 | Desmos / on-screen calc / highlight/flag/eliminator / whiteboard / OMR shading |
| Review & Synthesis (weekend re-solve every hard miss 2-3 ways) | 2 | Algebraic, tool-based, estimation — time each, slowest domain = next gain |

**Hard-question protocol for EvAU / Selectividad:** Re-solve every hard miss two to three ways. Time each — your slowest domain is your next 15-point/band gain. If EvAU / Selectividad is adaptive (section-level CAT), hard Section / hard items carry disproportionate weight — missing a hard item costs more than missing an easy one, but you only see hard items if you earn them — Section 1 is the gate. Treat every Section 1 question as gatekeeping.

**Vocabulary / Formula maintenance:** Continue spaced repetition — 10 min/day. For EvAU / Selectividad, this may be the difference between 6.5→7.0 or 60→70.

**Stamina:** For EvAU / Selectividad at Fase General (4-5 obligatorias) + Fase Especifica (hasta 4 optativas), 90m per examen total, practice seated duration monthly from month 2 — break simulation (10 min between sections) matters.

Q: Can I retake the EvAU / Selectividad quickly?

This is not "what to study" for EvAU / Selectividad — it is **how to execute on the hardest EvAU / Selectividad items** where competitive scores stall and where most preparation material is thinnest for University Entrance. At the top tier for EvAU / Selectividad (Fase General (4-5 obligatorias) + Fase Especifica (hasta 4 optativas), 90m per examen; 0-10 + 0-4 =14 max), every candidate knows the syllabus. ### The EvAU / Selectividad Hard-Question Reality

**What elite requires for EvAU / Selectividad (calibrated from official practice test 90th percentile):**
- Section 1 or equivalent (gate): ~85-90% correct to unlock hard/upper band and access 80th-plus percentile
- Hard Section / hardest 30%: ~75-80% correct for 90th percentile; ~90% for 99th
- Tool-solvable items (where EvAU / Selectividad allows aids): ~60% of hard items in <60 seconds with aid (Desmos, on-screen calculator, highlight/flag, whiteboard, formula sheet where provided)
- Careless error rate: <2 per full EvAU / Selectividad paper — at 90th percentile, 70% of misses are careless/timing/strategy, not content

**Implication:** If you are past content mastery for EvAU / Selectividad, your next 10 percentile points come from process, not syllabus — in particular, from 15-second extraction, logic-chain prediction, and pacing triage.

### Technique 1: 15-Second Visual Extraction Protocol (for any EvAU / Selectividad graph, passage, table, or diagram)

Graphs, passages, tables, and diagrams in EvAU / Selectividad test data reading, not recall. The text often merely describes the visual. Go to the visual. Drill this protocol until it is automatic for EvAU / Selectividad:

1. **Title & Axes (3 sec):** Variables, units, independent (x, horizontal) vs dependent (y, vertical). For EvAU / Selectividad, circle the units — many traps are unit mismatches (mm vs cm, 000 vs M, per hour vs per day).
2. **Trend & Scale (5 sec):** Linear, exponential, inverse, threshold/plateau, periodic, log scale (1, 10, 100 = log). For EvAU / Selectividad, note inflection points — where linear becomes plateau.
3. **Key Values (4 sec):** Peaks, intercepts, intersections, asymptotes, outliers, max/min — annotate on screen or scratch.
4. **Legend/Note & Sample Size (3 sec):** Series, conditions, treatments, n — sample size determines generalizability; treatments explain legend.

**Drill for EvAU / Selectividad:** 10 visuals per day (official bank + academic sources + University Entrance case studies), covering visuals only, then answering without reading text. Aim to answer 40% of EvAU / Selectividad questions from visuals alone — especially Data Representation, PS, QA word problems with figures, and science licensure items.

**Common visual trap for EvAU / Selectividad:** "Outside knowledge bait" — question sounds like it needs Biology/Chemistry/Physics for EvAU / Selectividad but answer is in the visual. If you are reaching for outside knowledge, re-scan.

---

### Technique 2: Logic-Chain Method (for EvAU / Selectividad text, argument, and reading items)

EvAU / Selectividad frequently tests **pivot words** that determine logical relationship: *however, although, because, since, therefore, on the other hand, for example, moreover, consequently, while, whereas, despite*.

**Protocol for EvAU / Selectividad:**
1. Find the pivot in the sentence/passage — it determines relationship (contrast, cause, example, condition, conclusion)
2. Predict the fill/answer before looking at options (cover choices)
3. Match prediction to choices — do not hunt synonyms; hunt **functional equivalence in context**
4. Trap in EvAU / Selectividad: synonyms that fit form but break logic are distractors — correct choice is often rephrased, not repeated word

**Example discipline for EvAU / Selectividad:** For vocabulary-in-context or text completion, define the needed *function* first: does the sentence need a positive word that continues, or a negative word that contrasts? Then find the word that performs that function — not the dictionary-best synonym.

**Additional for EvAU / Selectividad where integrated writing is tested:** Logic chain also governs Task Achievement: reading states X, lecture states not-X → your integrated essay must contrast, not summarize.

---

### Technique 3: Tool Superpowers (for EvAU / Selectividad where aids are allowed — master what you are given)

- **Desmos / On-screen calculator:** For EvAU / Selectividad where quantitative appears — system intersection method (graph both equations, read intersection), graphing for optimisation (vertex/zeros), regression (y1 ~ a*b^x1), stats (mean/SD via stats([...])), table for function evaluation. Master the 5 core workflows for EvAU / Selectividad; sub-60-second average on tool-solvable items buys 5-8 minutes for reasoning-heavy items on EvAU / Selectividad's tight timing (Fase General (4-5 obligatorias) + Fase Especifica (hasta 4 optativas), 90m per examen).
- **Highlighters / Flags / Answer Eliminator / Line Reader:** For EvAU / Selectividad where CBT — pre-mark pivots, axis labels, question stems; eliminate on screen; flag time-sinks; use line reader for dense tables.
- **Whiteboard / Erasable Sheet / Scratch Paper:** For EvAU / Selectividad where at-home/CBT — 2-column table for conflicting viewpoints or argument structure, quick sketches for geometry, matrix for multi-part analysis, checklist for word limits.

**Speed target for EvAU / Selectividad:** Sub-60-second average on the 50-60% of items that are tool-solvable — this is your time bank for the 20% hardest.

**Practice:** 10-minute daily tool/annotation drills until automatic — e.g., 5 systems via intersection, 3 regressions, 5 stats calculations for EvAU / Selectividad.

### Domain-Specific Hard Patterns for EvAU / Selectividad (University Entrance)

#### Foundational Domain (Largest Weight — Where Rank Is Built)

- Recognize disguised forms: EvAU / Selectividad word problems, modelling scenarios, multi-constraint systems that look like stories but reduce to equations
- Pattern: Translate (English → equation) -> Visualize (graph/table/sketch) -> Compute with tool -> Verify with alternate method (estimate vs calculation)
- Pitfalls for EvAU / Selectividad: Hidden constraints (integer, positive, domain), "must vs could" operator (must be true vs could be true), unit mismatch, mixed-number vs fraction entry

#### Advanced Domain (Differentiator — Where 80th → 90th Is Decided)

- Hybrid items combining 2-3 domains for EvAU / Selectividad (e.g., algebra + data, reasoning + evidence, science + data, ethics + communication)
- Pattern: Graph both sides of equation; count intersections; check domain restrictions (sqrt requires >=0, log requires >0, denominator non-zero)
- Pitfall: Extraneous solutions (squaring introduces roots that fail original), back-bonds / coordination number in inorganic for science exams, assumption strength vs sufficiency in reasoning

#### Analytical / Data Domain (High Yield, Lower Volume — Often Under-Practiced for EvAU / Selectividad)

- Ratios, percentages, conditional probability, distributions, correlation — high yield because candidates under-practice
- Pattern: Restrict denominator to condition ("Given X, probability of Y" → denominator = count of X only); watch "increase by" vs "increase to"; percent of percent
- Pitfall for EvAU / Selectividad: Observational data = correlation; only controlled experiments support causation; error bars overlapping = no significant difference

#### Writing / Communication Domain (Where Allowed for EvAU / Selectividad)

- Structure > vocabulary: 4 paragraphs (intro, point 1 + evidence, point 2 + counter, conclusion) beats a vocabulary dump
- Word limit and task achievement: overview paragraph (Writing Task 1 Academic for IELTS/TOEFL-integrated for PTE) = max Band 5 without it
- Citation vs opinion: Integrated tasks cite sources; independent tasks argue position with examples — mixing is penalised

### Pacing: The Hidden Gate for EvAU / Selectividad (Triage Is Mandatory)

Fase General (4-5 obligatorias) + Fase Especifica (hasta 4 optativas), 90m per examen implies tight average time per item for EvAU / Selectividad — typically 45-90 seconds. Use triage on first pass:

| Tag | Meaning for EvAU / Selectividad | Action | Time Budget |
|-----|----------------------|--------|-------------|
| **GREEN** | Confident, quick — know domain and operator | Solve immediately | 30-60 sec |
| **YELLOW** | Know how, multi-step or 15-sec extraction needed | Flag, second pass | 90-120 sec |
| **RED** | No clear path, trap-heavy, or 3-visual synthesis | Guess, mark, move — return only if time | 20-30 sec |

**First pass for EvAU / Selectividad:** All GREEN (60% of paper) in ~50% time → builds score and confidence.
**Second pass:** YELLOW with fresh eyes.
**Last 3 minutes:** Guesses/reviews for RED; check OMR darkening/entry format.

**At elite levels for EvAU / Selectividad, not attempting a RED is a feature, not a failure** — it preserves time for 3 GREENs that guarantee points.

---

### Error Elimination Checklist (Every Question, 5 Seconds, for EvAU / Selectividad)

- Re-read the stem after solving — what is *asked*? (x vs y, increase vs decrease, radius vs diameter, per year vs per month, 000 vs M, "which does NOT")
- Units: per hour vs per day, per year vs per month, absolute vs percent, 000 vs M, mm vs cm
- Entry format: fraction vs decimal vs percent vs word limit (e.g., "NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER" for IELTS; "TITA" for CAT; "NAT" range for GATE)
- Darkening / Transfer: OMR 1 per row; CBT check review screen for unanswered vs flagged
- Tool verification: quick graphical/estimation check for algebraic answer for EvAU / Selectividad — does the number make sense?

### Practice Protocol for EvAU / Selectividad Mastery (Weeks 5-10)

**Weekly (Weeks 5-8):**
- Hard question sets (top 25% official pool for EvAU / Selectividad, filtered by hard flag) timed per section — 20 questions in 30 min
- Post-test: Categorize every miss (Content / Careless / Timing / Strategy) — at elite, 70% are Careless/Timing/Strategy, so fix process
- Daily: 10-minute tool/annotation drills for EvAU / Selectividad until automatic — e.g., 5 graph extractions, 3 systems, 5 logic-chain predictions

**Bi-weekly:** Full EvAU / Selectividad section under time, with break simulation (10 min between sections). Track checkpoint times at Q10, Q20, Q30 vs target.

**Final week:** No new hard sets — re-solve past hard misses; confidence > novelty for EvAU / Selectividad.

Bottom line for EvAU / Selectividad: Content gets you to competitive (70th percentile). Execution — 15-second extraction, logic-chain prediction, and triage — gets you to elite (90th). Drill the protocols until they are automatic for EvAU / Selectividad.

The score report shows numbers, but not what to *do* with them for admissions, licensure, placement, scholarships, or retakes. This guide translates your EvAU / Selectividad report into strategy for the 2024-2025 cycle — verifiable against Ministry of Education (Spain) + Universities's official score interpretation and your 8-12 specific target programmes' published statistics.

---

### Understanding Your EvAU / Selectividad Score Report

**Primary Score(s):** 0-10 + 0-4 =14 max
**What the report contains:** Total/overall, section/component scores, percentile vs recent cohort, validity dates, verification number (TRF/registration number), and sometimes subscores or proficiency levels (e.g., CEFR for English, deciles for UCAT, bands for IELTS/PTE/CELPIP, scaled + subscores for GRE).

| Report Component | Example for EvAU / Selectividad | How Institutions/Employers Use It |
|------------------|---------------------|-------------------------------------|
| **Total / Overall** | 0-10 + 0-4 =14 max (e.g., 7.0, 650, AIR 5000, 300/400) | Primary filter for merit lists, cutoffs, scholarships — overall threshold |
| **Section / Component** | Per-skill/seat (e.g., Reading 7.5, Quant 48, Paper 1 90/180) | Used for sectional cutoffs — **failing a section disqualifies even if overall high** (common in India, UK, Canada, Australia: CAT sectional 80, UCAT SJT, IELTS no less than 6.0, PTE no less than 58, CELPIP CLB) |
| **Subscores / Profiles** | Diagnostic breakdown (e.g., CEFR B2, UCAT decile, CFA topic band) | Often NOT used for admissions; diagnostic for your preparation only — do not over-index |
| **Percentile / Rank** | vs recent cohort (nationally representative vs test-taker pool) | Context for "how competitive is 1200 vs 1350?" — test-taker percentile (vs actual takers) is what competitive programmes see |

**Percentiles — two contexts you must distinguish for EvAU / Selectividad:**
- **Nationally representative percentile:** vs all eligible candidates (including non-takers) — higher numbers (e.g., 1200 SAT ~ 75th nationally)
- **Test-taker pool percentile:** vs actual EvAU / Selectividad takers — lower numbers, more relevant for competitive programmes (e.g., 1200 SAT ~ 65th among takers) — this is what admissions file readers see in the US undergraduate context; other contexts similar

**Reporting timeline & validity for EvAU / Selectividad:**
- Digital/CBT: often **2-5 days** (e.g., TOEFL iBT 4-13 days, IELTS computer 3-5 days, PTE 48h, Duolingo 48h, GMAT Focus 3-5 days, GRE 8-10 days)
- Paper: **2-3 weeks** (e.g., IELTS paper 13 days, UPSC prelims ~10 days)
- At-home/Online: similar to digital
- Validity: **2 years** for English proficiency (for visas — UKVI/Australia Home Affairs/IRCC enforce 2-year-at-entry) or **2-5 years** for admissions/licensure (e.g., GRE/GMAT/MCAT 3-5 years, JEE Advanced rank only that year) — verify your programme's "valid at course start" definition, not just test date

**Score verification for EvAU / Selectividad:** TRF/registration/AR number verifiable online (e.g., IELTS TRF verification at ieltsverification.org, ETS/GMAC at ets.org/mba.com verification, NTA via DigiLocker, UPSC marksheet).

### What Is 'Good' for EvAU / Selectividad? — Program-Specific, Not Universal

There is no universal "good" for EvAU / Selectividad. There is only "competitive for YOUR targets." A 1200 SAT is competitive for a regional public and uncompetitive for an Ivy; a 7.0 IELTS is competitive for Canada CLB 9 and uncompetitive for Oxford. Same for every EvAU / Selectividad.

#### The Middle 50% / Median / Cutoff Rule for EvAU / Selectividad

1. List your 8-12 targets (reach: admit rate <15% or AIR <1000; match: 15-40% or AIR 1000-10000; safety: >40% or qualifying + margin). For EvAU / Selectividad, targets are programmes, institutions, licensing boards, or immigration streams.
2. For each target, find its published **middle 50% (25th-75th)** or **median/AIR/cutoff** or **previous-year cut-off** or **previous-year departmental cutoff** for EvAU / Selectividad — search "[Exact Institution + Exact Programme] + EvAU / Selectividad + Common Data Set / admission statistics / previous-year cut-off / departmental marks / AIR / NTA score / UCAT decile" for the most recent completed cycle (not 3 years ago).
3. Goal for EvAU / Selectividad:
   - **Safety / licensure qualifying:** at/above **75th percentile** (or pass threshold + margin, e.g., +5-10 points/bands, or +0.5 band for IELTS, +100 rank buffer for JEE/NEET)
   - **Match:** at/above **75th** for overall competitiveness
   - **Reach:** at/above **median (50th)** is minimum viable; below 25th is uncompetitive

#### Example Tiers — Verify Current 2024-2025 Data for EvAU / Selectividad (Illustrative)

| Tier | Example Programme Type for EvAU / Selectividad | Typical EvAU / Selectividad Range / Threshold | Target (at this tier for EvAU / Selectividad) |
|------|-------------------------------------|------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| **Most Selective** | Top global/health/law/finance/engineering/Ivy/M7 | Top 5-10% of EvAU / Selectividad distribution (e.g., Ivy/M7, AIIMS Delhi, IIT Bombay CSE) | 90th+ percentile or AIR 1-100 |
| **Highly Selective** | Strong national/regional flagships, Top 20-40 globally | Top 25% (e.g., UCLA/Vandy/USC, IIM-K, NIT Trichy, SKY) | 75th+ percentile |
| **Selective** | Mid-tier universities / qualifying boards with margin | Average+ (e.g., state medical ~610 NEET, SSC CGL Tier 1 ~150, CAT ~85th) | Above median of admitted |
| **Qualifying** | Licensure/entry threshold | Pass mark (e.g., CPA 75, NCLEX pass, FE pass, C+ KCSE) | Pass + margin (+5-10% to account for equating) |

**For University Entrance with EvAU / Selectividad, sectional thresholds dominate:** e.g., UK/Australia English: "Overall 7.0 with no sub-test below 6.5/6.0" for IELTS/PTE/TOEFL/CELPIP; India: "Sectional 80-85 for CAT; 10% per subject for JEE Advanced; 50th percentile overall for NEET qualifying but 600+ for government seat; UCAT SJT Band 1-2 for interview; JAMB departmental 250-320 for Medicine/Law".

### Superscore / ScoreSelect / Score Choice / Revaluation for EvAU / Selectividad

Policy varies more by **institution/counselling body** than by test:

| Policy | What It Means for EvAU / Selectividad | What You Should Send for EvAU / Selectividad |
|--------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| **Superscore** | Best section scores across dates recombined into new total/average (e.g., SAT/ACT superscore, GRE informal) | All dates where you have a best section — institution calculates |
| **Highest Single Sitting** | Best overall in one sitting only — sections not mixed | Single best date only for EvAU / Selectividad |
| **All Scores Required** | Institution sees every sitting (e.g., Georgetown/Yale for SAT/ACT, some medical schools) | All dates (no choice) — retake only if upward trend likely |
| **Test-Blind / Test-Optional** | Score not used or optional (e.g., UC system test-blind, many post-COVID flexible) | Optional submit — submit if at/above median; withhold if below 25th where non-test profile compensates |
| **Revaluation / One Skill Retake / Enquiry / EOR** | EvAU / Selectividad-specific: Ministry of Education (Spain) + Universities may offer remarking (e.g., IELTS EOR, UPSC RTI copy), One Skill Retake (IELTS OSR within 60 days), MyBest (TOEFL) — verify if YOUR institution/counselling (JoSAA/MCC/CAP/UCA) accepts retooled scores | Check per counselling body — e.g., IELTS OSR accepted by 1,200+ orgs as of 2024 but not Oxbridge/medicine; TOEFL MyBest by 90% US but not some UK |

**General strategy for EvAU / Selectividad:**
- For **superscore institutions** -> send all dates where you have a best section — they calculate the best composite
- For **highest single sitting** -> send single best EvAU / Selectividad date only
- For **test-optional/test-blind** -> submit if at/above median for that institution; withhold if below 25th where essays/GPA/work/portfolio compensates
- For **immigration (CELPIP/IELTS/PTE/CELPIP)**: IRCC/Australia Home Affairs/UKVI do NOT superscore — threshold must be met in one sitting

### Retake Decision Framework for EvAU / Selectividad — Is Another Sitting Worth It?

#### Expected Gain on Retake for EvAU / Selectividad (Illustrative, varies by preparation quality)

| Preparation Level for EvAU / Selectividad | Typical Gain | With Domain/Gating Fix (highest ROI) |
|-------------------------------|--------------|----------------------------------------|
| **Light (10-20h, informal)** | +2 to +5% (or +0.5 band / +3-5 scaled points / +500-1000 rank improvement rank-dependent) | +5-8% on focused section |
| **Serious (40+ hours, targeted on weakest 2 domains, official materials)** | +5 to +10% (or +0.5-1.0 band / +10-20 scaled points / +2000-5000 rank) | +10-15% if gating or access to hard difficulty/sectional cutoff fixed |
| **Gating Fix (unlocking hard Section 2, fixing time management, overcoming word-limit penalties)** | +8 to +15% on total — single largest ROI for EvAU / Selectividad | Frontier gain |

**For EvAU / Selectividad with hard cutoffs:** Retake ROI is binary — 0.5 band / 10 scaled points below = zero for automatic merit (e.g., UKVI, CLB, scholarship) while 0.5/10 above = threshold met + funding.

#### Decision Tree for EvAU / Selectividad

```
Is score below 25th percentile (or below sectional cutoff) for ALL targets/counselling cutoffs?
  -> YES -> Retake + broaden institution/counselling list to include matches where you are already 75th+
Is one section >=1.3 SD below the others (e.g., Quant 8.0 but Writing 6.0 for IELTS)?
  -> YES -> Section-specific preparation (not full retake prep) -> Retake — highest ROI per hour for EvAU / Selectividad
Is score in 25th-75th for top-choice target?
  -> Do you have 6-8 weeks before deadline/counselling with 12h/week available?
     -> YES -> Targeted preparation on highest-weight weak domain for EvAU / Selectividad -> Retake
     -> NO  -> Do not retake; submit and strengthen other components (essays, work, portfolio) — marginal gain not worth opportunity cost
Is score >75th for top-choice target?
  -> Only retake for specific scholarship/fellowship cutoff (often +0.5 band / +10-20 scaled points = USD 10k-30k/year) or if rank can improve into higher scholarship band
Undecided for EvAU / Selectividad?
  -> Take 1 official full practice test under full conditions including timing/breaks: if practice >5% above real score (or +0.5 band), retake; if within 3%, do not — variance
```

**Retake constraints for EvAU / Selectividad:**
- Waiting period: 3 days for TOEFL/IELTS/PTE/DET, 21 days for GRE, 16 days for GMAT Focus, 1-7 days for many Indian CBTs (check Ministry of Education (Spain) + Universities)
- Attempt limits: 5 per 12 months for GMAT/GRE, 3 per year for LSAT, 2 consecutive years for JEE Advanced, unlimited for many
- Delivery: Can switch paper <-> computer between sittings (where offered) — choose delivery that suits your practice

**Cost of retake for EvAU / Selectividad:** Full fee again (or OSR at 65% for IELTS) + opportunity cost of 40-60 preparation hours — compare to funding gain.

### Funding / Placement / Licensure Nuances Specific to EvAU / Selectividad (University Entrance)

- **Scholarships/Fellowships have hard cutoffs for EvAU / Selectividad:** For EvAU / Selectividad, 0.5 band / 10 scaled points / 500 ranks below = zero for automatic merit, while above = threshold met. Example searches for EvAU / Selectividad: "[Exact Institution] merit scholarship + EvAU / Selectividad cutoff 2024" or "[Country] scholarship + EvAU / Selectividad CLB/band 2024" — retake ROI can be 10k-30k per year, far exceeding test fee.
- **Course placement:** Some institutions use EvAU / Selectividad section scores for placement (e.g., math for calculus, Writing for freshman composition, English for foundation vs direct entry) — a Band 7 Writing or 650 English may waive a prerequisite semester.
- **Licensure/inspection:** Some boards set higher-than-pass for tiered recognition or interstate mobility (e.g., bar admission on motion with higher UBE, interstate nursing licensure with higher NCLEX margin, PSU interview with higher GATE score + experience).

FAQ:

Q: How long are EvAU / Selectividad scores valid?
A: Typically 2 years for English proficiency, 5 years for admissions/licensure - verify with your programs.

Q: Can I retake the EvAU / Selectividad quickly?
A: Most administrations enforce a waiting period and attempt limits per year. Most improve 5-15% with 40+ hours targeted preparation.

Q: Do schools/employers superscore EvAU / Selectividad?
A: Varies by institution and exam. Many admissions programs superscore; licensure rarely does. Check each program's policy.

Q: Is EvAU / Selectividad required for all programs?
A: Many programs are test-optional, but a strong score still helps for merit aid or qualification. Verify each program's requirement.

Q: How do I choose between EvAU / Selectividad and alternatives?
A: Take one official diagnostic of each, compare percentiles, and apply the decision matrix in the comparison article.

Q: What is a competitive score for top programs?
A: At or above the 75th percentile for your target's published admitted range. Search program admission statistics for the most recent cycle.

FULL ARTICLE:

The TEAS (Test of Essential Academic Skills) - ATI is a high-stakes gate within Nursing Entrance — administered by ATI and taken by tens to hundreds of thousands annually to determine admission, progression, or licensure. Unlike low-stakes internal exams, TEAS 7 is **externally validated, scaled, and normed**: your score is compared against a national/international cohort, not just your class. This guide explains the live 2024-2025 format with verified timing, question distribution, ID rules, and centre logistics so you arrive with zero surprises.

---

### What Is the TEAS 7 and Who Needs It?

**Core purpose:** Measure the competencies your target institution or regulator has defined as prerequisite for success — whether academic readiness, professional judgment, or language proficiency for study/work/migration.

**Take TEAS 7 if:**
- Your 8-12 specific target institutions, employers, or immigration streams **explicitly list TEAS 7** as accepted/required (check each programme page: "Accepted tests: TEAS 7" — not just a generic testing page)
- You need a portable, externally verified score for merit scholarships, visas, or multi-country applications
- Your diagnostic percentile on TEAS 7 is higher than on alternatives

**You may not need TEAS 7 if:**
- Your targets are **test-optional/test-blind** and your non-test profile (GPA, work, portfolio) is already at 75th percentile
- An alternative test is accepted equally and your alternative diagnostic is higher
- You qualify for an exemption (e.g., English-medium degree waiver for English tests, prior licensure)

**Decision before booking:** Screenshot the exact line from your target's admissions/immigration page: "TEAS 7 — minimum ...". Generic "English test required" is not enough — confirm TEAS 7 by name.

---

### Format at a Glance (2024-2025 Verified)

| Component | Duration / Questions | What Is Tested | Delivery Detail |
|-----------|---------------------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Overall** | 170q (150 scored), 209m: Reading 45q, Math 38q, Science 50q, English 37q | Domain-specific content per Nursing Entrance | 0-100% per section + composite |
| **Primary Section(s)** | See official bulletin for TEAS 7 (distribution varies by form/session) | Applied reasoning and knowledge synthesis | Check official specifications for section-level adaptivity vs linear |
| **Secondary / Integrated** | Varies by paper/elective/specialism | Communication, professional judgment, data interpretation | Integrated tasks where applicable |

**Key 2024-2025 changes for TEAS 7:**
- Digital/CBT is now primary in most regions — verify paper vs computer vs at-home for your centre (some regions phased out paper)
- Scoring scale stable (0-100% per section + composite) but percentile tables shift annually — use 2024 table for interpretation
- Calculator and aid policies updated — see "Tools" below
- Validity 2-3 years for language/immigration, 3-5 years for admissions/licensure — confirm with regulator

**Tools (allowed aids) for TEAS 7:**
- Calculator: Check official calculator policy (on-screen for many CBTs; physical where allowed must be approved model — e.g., no CAS, no QWERTY, no paper tape)
- Reference: Formula sheet for some (e.g., SAT, FE) vs no sheet for others (e.g., GATE, JEE Advanced, CFA) — know before you memorise
- Rough work: Whiteboard/erasable sheet for at-home/CBT (1 sheet in sheet protector) vs scratch paper at centre

---

### Section-by-Section Deep Dive for TEAS 7

#### Primary Domain (Largest Weight — Where Rank Is Decided)

**Why it matters:** The primary domain contributes 35-50% of your total/score. For TEAS 7, this is where 80th vs 90th percentile is decided. Example patterns:
- Knowledge-recall items (20-30%): Direct definition or formula — free if memorised, lost if not
- Comprehension items (30-40%): Apply concept to passage/data — requires reading, not recall
- Analysis items (20-30%): Synthesize 2-3 concepts — the differentiator; requires multi-step reasoning
- Evaluation items (10%): Judge sufficiency or best argument — hardest; requires logic

**Hard-item preview for TEAS 7:**
- Item with 3-4 concept integration (e.g., thermodynamics + equilibrium + kinetics)
- Item requiring graph extraction in 15 seconds + calculation
- Item with trap operator: NOT, EXCEPT, LEAST, CANNOT, MUST vs COULD

**Strategy:** Master the 3 most frequent sub-types in this domain first — they yield 60% of points.

#### Secondary Domain(s)

**Data/Analytical:** Ratios, conditional probability, distribution, correlation — restrict denominator to condition; watch units; correlation with observational data is not causation (only experiments with controls support causation).

**Communication:** Synthesis across sources — identify pivot words (however, although, because, therefore), predict answer before options, match functional equivalence not synonym.

**Integrated/Case:** Evolving item types in licensure (NCLEX NGN, UCAT SJT, CFA ethics) — practice with official sample items, not third-party.

### Registration: Step-by-Step for TEAS 7 (2024-2025)

#### 1. Create Official Account
Use ATI's portal. Enter legal name exactly as on government ID/passport (including middle name, hyphen, diacritics). This account is permanent — use a personal email you will retain.

#### 2. Verify Eligibility Before Paying
- Education: degree level, board, percentage/percentile, caregory certificate format (central vs state)
- Age: lower and upper bounds, and date-of-reference
- Attempts: max per year/lifetime (e.g., JEE Advanced 2 consecutive, GMAT 5 per 12 months)
- Documents: photo (80% face), signature, thumb, ID number, self-declaration where required

#### 3. Choose Delivery, Date, and City
- **Test dates:** Book 6-10 weeks ahead for preferred dates; peak (Sep-Nov, Jan-Mar, May for Indian exams) fills 2 months early. International centres fill 2-3 months ahead.
- **Cities:** Choose 3-8 preferences; allotment by computer — you may not get first choice in peak.
- **At-home (where offered):** Verify technical (OS, browser, lockdown, camera, mic) and environment (private room, door closed, clear desk, whiteboard only) **2 weeks before** — do the official system check.

#### 4. Provide Information and Score Recipients
- High school/university codes, photo upload, intended programmes, background questionnaire (optional but used for search/scholarships)
- Score recipients: 4-5 free if listed within 1 month of test (check free TRF/report policy for TEAS 7); additional ~USD/GBP 20-35 each.

#### 5. Pay and Confirm
- Fee varies by country/category — check ATI for your country (fees adjust 2x/year) — screenshot confirmation.
- Confirmation email + reference number saved — needed for admit card and TRF verification.

**Fee reduction:** Many TEAS 7 administrations offer need-based waivers (e.g., ACT/SAT/GRE/GMAT fee waivers for low-income, GATE/CEED SC/ST waiver) — apply 4-6 weeks before intended test.

#### 6. Download Admit / Confirm Centre
Admit / city slip 1-2 weeks before → check reporting time (often 30 min before gate closes). Visit centre if unfamiliar — reduce test-day anxiety.

### Scoring for TEAS 7: How Your 0-100% per section + composite Is Calculated

**Scale:** 0-100% per section + composite — scaled, not raw. Two candidates with same raw can have different scaled due to equating (form difficulty) or adaptivity weighting.

**Percentiles:** Annual, based on recent cohort (e.g., 2023-2024 test-taker pool). Your test-taker percentile (vs actual takers) is what competitive programmes see; nationally representative (vs all eligible) is higher.

**Cutoffs/Criteria:**
- Fixed benchmark (e.g., 75 to pass for CPA, C for A-Level, C+ for KCSE, 50th percentile for NEET qualifying)
- Rank-based (e.g., JEE Advanced, GATE, CAT, UCAT deciles, JAMB departmental) — rank, not marks, determines seat
- Sectional + overall (e.g., CAT 80 sectional, UCAT SJT Band 1-2) — failing a section = no offer even if overall high

**Reporting timeline:** Digital/CBT often 2-5 days; paper 2-3 weeks; validity 2 years (language for visas) or 3-5 years (admissions) — check your programme's "valid at course start" definition.

**Score verification:** TRF/registration number verifiable online (e.g., IELTS TRF verification, ETS/GMAC score verification).

### Test Day: What to Bring, What to Expect at the Centre

**Required:** Admit + same ID as registration (passport for most international; government/school ID where allowed — UKVI/CELPIP/IELTS for UKVI always passport) + TRN/reference + transparent water bottle.

**Prohibited:** Phones (off and in locker — touching during break = disqualified), watches (including analogue), notes, food (except at designated break), unauthorised calculators.

**Centre experience (typical 08:00-15:00 for paper, shorter for CBT):**
07:30 Check-in (ID, photo, biometrics — finger/palm, bag in locker)
08:30 Tutorial + Section 1(s) — no pause within timed sections
11:00 Break (10-30 min, designated area only)
11:30 Section 2(s)
13:00 Survey + unofficial scores if provided
**CBT nuance:** Headphones provided, highlight/flag/eliminator on screen, 2-min review at end (no extra transfer like paper Listening).

### Official Practice Resources — The Only Authentic Predictor

**Free (start here, on ATI portal):**
- Official practice test (1-2 full tests free) — diagnostic gold
- Sample questions with answers and band descriptors / scoring guides
- Preparation portal/app with timed practice

**Paid (use after free — in order of authenticity):**
- Official guide (3-6 authentic past tests) — e.g., Cambridge IELTS 10-19 (10 tests), Official GMAT Guide (900 Qs), AAMC FLs (4), LSAC PrepTests (70+)
- Official online practice (computer simulation with timer)
- Official coaching/live online (mock Speaking / interview where applicable)

**Sequence:** Diagnostic (full, timed, 2.5-3h) → score per section using official table → identify weakest 2 sections → targeted practice (hardest items first) → Test 2 → Test 3 the week before.

**Do NOT:** Use non-official practice for score prediction — difficulty is inflated/deflated and adaptive algorithm not replicated.

### International Candidate Notes for TEAS 7

- **Centre choice:** Competing networks (e.g., British Council vs IDP for IELTS, NTA vs TCS iON for Indian exams) — same test, choose closer/cheaper/earlier date.
- **Retake:** Waiting period varies (3 days TOEFL/IELTS, 21 days GRE, 16 days GMAT Focus, 1 day for many Indian CBTs) — unlimited for most but cost; some adjust superscore/OSR (e.g., IELTS One Skill Retake within 60 days — check if YOUR institution accepts OSR; many UK/Australia do, some Oxbridge/US do not).
- **Visa vs admission:** English tests for admission vs for visa (UKVI, Australia Home Affairs, IRCC) may differ — a standard TRF may be invalid for visa. Verify with immigration authority, not just university.

### Frequently Asked Questions for TEAS 7

**Q: Can I take TEAS 7 on paper vs computer?**
A: Many TEAS 7 administrations are now digital/CBT primary; paper remains in some regions or for accommodations. At-home exists for select tests. Verify with official bulletin for your country/centre — do not assume.

**Q: How many times can I take it?**
A: Attempt limits vary (e.g., 2 attempts/consecutive years for JEE Advanced, 5 per 12 months for GMAT/GRE, unlimited for IELTS/TOEFL/PTE but cost). Most candidates take 1-3 times; schools/regulators see only scores you elect to send but some require all.

**Q: What is a 'good' score for TEAS 7?**
A: No universal threshold. It is 'at/above 75th percentile for your safety/match targets, at/above median for reach'. Search "[Institution/Course] + TEAS 7 + Common Data Set / admission statistics / previous-year cutoff" for the most recent cycle — that is your target.

**Q: When should I start preparing for TEAS 7?**
A: Ideal 8-12 weeks for focused preparation; minimum 4-6 weeks intensive. Diagnostic first — do not build a plan without baseline + timing data.

**Q: Does TEAS 7 have negative marking?**
A: Check marking scheme per question type: MCQ -1/3 to -1, TITA/NAT 0, multiple-correct partial credit — changes guessing strategy.

### Key Takeaways for TEAS 7

1. **Format digital/CBT in most regions** — verify paper/computer/at-home for your centre.
2. **Scoring 0-100% per section + composite** — percentile, not raw, determines competitiveness.
3. **Official practice tests are the only authentic predictor** — prioritize them over any third-party.

### The TEAS 7 Hard-Question Reality

**What elite requires for TEAS 7 (calibrated from official practice test 90th percentile):**
- Section 1 or equivalent (gate): ~85-90% correct to unlock hard/upper band and access 80th-plus percentile
- Hard Section / hardest 30%: ~75-80% correct for 90th percentile; ~90% for 99th
- Tool-solvable items (where TEAS 7 allows aids): ~60% of hard items in <60 seconds with aid (Desmos, on-screen calculator, highlight/flag, whiteboard, formula sheet where provided)
- Careless error rate: <2 per full TEAS 7 paper — at 90th percentile, 70% of misses are careless/timing/strategy, not content

**Implication:** If you are past content mastery for TEAS 7, your next 10 percentile points come from process, not syllabus — in particular, from 15-second extraction, logic-chain prediction, and pacing triage.

---

### Technique 1: 15-Second Visual Extraction Protocol (for any TEAS 7 graph, passage, table, or diagram)

Graphs, passages, tables, and diagrams in TEAS 7 test data reading, not recall. The text often merely describes the visual. Go to the visual. Drill this protocol until it is automatic for TEAS 7:

1. **Title & Axes (3 sec):** Variables, units, independent (x, horizontal) vs dependent (y, vertical). For TEAS 7, circle the units — many traps are unit mismatches (mm vs cm, 000 vs M, per hour vs per day).
2. **Trend & Scale (5 sec):** Linear, exponential, inverse, threshold/plateau, periodic, log scale (1, 10, 100 = log). For TEAS 7, note inflection points — where linear becomes plateau.
3. **Key Values (4 sec):** Peaks, intercepts, intersections, asymptotes, outliers, max/min — annotate on screen or scratch.
4. **Legend/Note & Sample Size (3 sec):** Series, conditions, treatments, n — sample size determines generalizability; treatments explain legend.

**Drill for TEAS 7:** 10 visuals per day (official bank + academic sources + Nursing Entrance case studies), covering visuals only, then answering without reading text. Aim to answer 40% of TEAS 7 questions from visuals alone — especially Data Representation, PS, QA word problems with figures, and science licensure items.

**Common visual trap for TEAS 7:** "Outside knowledge bait" — question sounds like it needs Biology/Chemistry/Physics for TEAS 7 but answer is in the visual. If you are reaching for outside knowledge, re-scan.

---

### Technique 2: Logic-Chain Method (for TEAS 7 text, argument, and reading items)

TEAS 7 frequently tests **pivot words** that determine logical relationship: *however, although, because, since, therefore, on the other hand, for example, moreover, consequently, while, whereas, despite*.

**Protocol for TEAS 7:**
1. Find the pivot in the sentence/passage — it determines relationship (contrast, cause, example, condition, conclusion)
2. Predict the fill/answer before looking at options (cover choices)
3. Match prediction to choices — do not hunt synonyms; hunt **functional equivalence in context**
4. Trap in TEAS 7: synonyms that fit form but break logic are distractors — correct choice is often rephrased, not repeated word

**Example discipline for TEAS 7:** For vocabulary-in-context or text completion, define the needed *function* first: does the sentence need a positive word that continues, or a negative word that contrasts? Then find the word that performs that function — not the dictionary-best synonym.

**Additional for TEAS 7 where integrated writing is tested:** Logic chain also governs Task Achievement: reading states X, lecture states not-X → your integrated essay must contrast, not summarize.

---

### Technique 3: Tool Superpowers (for TEAS 7 where aids are allowed — master what you are given)

- **Desmos / On-screen calculator:** For TEAS 7 where quantitative appears — system intersection method (graph both equations, read intersection), graphing for optimisation (vertex/zeros), regression (y1 ~ a*b^x1), stats (mean/SD via stats([...])), table for function evaluation. Master the 5 core workflows for TEAS 7; sub-60-second average on tool-solvable items buys 5-8 minutes for reasoning-heavy items on TEAS 7's tight timing (170q (150 scored), 209m: Reading 45q, Math 38q, Science 50q, English 37q).
- **Highlighters / Flags / Answer Eliminator / Line Reader:** For TEAS 7 where CBT — pre-mark pivots, axis labels, question stems; eliminate on screen; flag time-sinks; use line reader for dense tables.
- **Whiteboard / Erasable Sheet / Scratch Paper:** For TEAS 7 where at-home/CBT — 2-column table for conflicting viewpoints or argument structure, quick sketches for geometry, matrix for multi-part analysis, checklist for word limits.

**Speed target for TEAS 7:** Sub-60-second average on the 50-60% of items that are tool-solvable — this is your time bank for the 20% hardest.

**Practice:** 10-minute daily tool/annotation drills until automatic — e.g., 5 systems via intersection, 3 regressions, 5 stats calculations for TEAS 7.

### Domain-Specific Hard Patterns for TEAS 7 (Nursing Entrance)

#### Foundational Domain (Largest Weight — Where Rank Is Built)

- Recognize disguised forms: TEAS 7 word problems, modelling scenarios, multi-constraint systems that look like stories but reduce to equations
- Pattern: Translate (English → equation) -> Visualize (graph/table/sketch) -> Compute with tool -> Verify with alternate method (estimate vs calculation)
- Pitfalls for TEAS 7: Hidden constraints (integer, positive, domain), "must vs could" operator (must be true vs could be true), unit mismatch, mixed-number vs fraction entry

#### Advanced Domain (Differentiator — Where 80th → 90th Is Decided)

- Hybrid items combining 2-3 domains for TEAS 7 (e.g., algebra + data, reasoning + evidence, science + data, ethics + communication)
- Pattern: Graph both sides of equation; count intersections; check domain restrictions (sqrt requires >=0, log requires >0, denominator non-zero)
- Pitfall: Extraneous solutions (squaring introduces roots that fail original), back-bonds / coordination number in inorganic for science exams, assumption strength vs sufficiency in reasoning

#### Analytical / Data Domain (High Yield, Lower Volume — Often Under-Practiced for TEAS 7)

- Ratios, percentages, conditional probability, distributions, correlation — high yield because candidates under-practice
- Pattern: Restrict denominator to condition ("Given X, probability of Y" → denominator = count of X only); watch "increase by" vs "increase to"; percent of percent
- Pitfall for TEAS 7: Observational data = correlation; only controlled experiments support causation; error bars overlapping = no significant difference

#### Writing / Communication Domain (Where Allowed for TEAS 7)

- Structure > vocabulary: 4 paragraphs (intro, point 1 + evidence, point 2 + counter, conclusion) beats a vocabulary dump
- Word limit and task achievement: overview paragraph (Writing Task 1 Academic for IELTS/TOEFL-integrated for PTE) = max Band 5 without it
- Citation vs opinion: Integrated tasks cite sources; independent tasks argue position with examples — mixing is penalised

### Pacing: The Hidden Gate for TEAS 7 (Triage Is Mandatory)

170q (150 scored), 209m: Reading 45q, Math 38q, Science 50q, English 37q implies tight average time per item for TEAS 7 — typically 45-90 seconds. Use triage on first pass:

| Tag | Meaning for TEAS 7 | Action | Time Budget |
|-----|----------------------|--------|-------------|
| **GREEN** | Confident, quick — know domain and operator | Solve immediately | 30-60 sec |
| **YELLOW** | Know how, multi-step or 15-sec extraction needed | Flag, second pass | 90-120 sec |
| **RED** | No clear path, trap-heavy, or 3-visual synthesis | Guess, mark, move — return only if time | 20-30 sec |

**First pass for TEAS 7:** All GREEN (60% of paper) in ~50% time → builds score and confidence.
**Second pass:** YELLOW with fresh eyes.
**Last 3 minutes:** Guesses/reviews for RED; check OMR darkening/entry format.

**At elite levels for TEAS 7, not attempting a RED is a feature, not a failure** — it preserves time for 3 GREENs that guarantee points.

---

### Error Elimination Checklist (Every Question, 5 Seconds, for TEAS 7)

- Re-read the stem after solving — what is *asked*? (x vs y, increase vs decrease, radius vs diameter, per year vs per month, 000 vs M, "which does NOT")
- Units: per hour vs per day, per year vs per month, absolute vs percent, 000 vs M, mm vs cm
- Entry format: fraction vs decimal vs percent vs word limit (e.g., "NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER" for IELTS; "TITA" for CAT; "NAT" range for GATE)
- Darkening / Transfer: OMR 1 per row; CBT check review screen for unanswered vs flagged
- Tool verification: quick graphical/estimation check for algebraic answer for TEAS 7 — does the number make sense?

**Weekly (Weeks 5-8):**
- Hard question sets (top 25% official pool for TEAS 7, filtered by hard flag) timed per section — 20 questions in 30 min

**Final week:** No new hard sets — re-solve past hard misses; confidence > novelty for TEAS 7.

Bottom line for TEAS 7: Content gets you to competitive (70th percentile). Execution — 15-second extraction, logic-chain prediction, and triage — gets you to elite (90th). Drill the protocols until they are automatic for TEAS 7.

### When TEAS 7 Is Stronger — Choose TEAS 7 If 3+ Apply

- **Diagnostic percentile on TEAS 7 is >=10 points higher than alternative** when both diagnostics taken same week under official conditions (official practice test, timed, same delivery)

### When the Alternative Is Stronger

Choose alternative if its structure suits your pace and cognitive profile, your alternative diagnostic is higher, or alternative is cheaper/more available in your city.

### Admissions / Licensure / Immigration Reality Check for TEAS 7

**Myth:** "Schools/boards/preferred country prefers one test"

**Fact:** Varies by institution, not by test. Some superscore (best sections across dates), some require all dates, some are test-blind (e.g., certain state systems or UKVI), some accept One Skill Retake/MyBest and some do not — verify per institution's testing policy page for 2024-2025 (e.g., IELTS One Skill Retake accepted by 1,200+ organisations as of 2024 but not Oxbridge; TOEFL MyBest accepted by 90% of US but not some UK).

**Myth:** "Test-optional = do not take TEAS 7"
**Fact:** Test-optional = submit if at/above median for your target; withhold if below 25th percentile where your non-test profile (GPA, work, portfolio, interview) compensates. Strong scores still help for merit aid, fellowships, and visa even when optional for admission.

### Understanding Your TEAS 7 Score Report

**Primary Score(s):** 0-100% per section + composite
**What the report contains:** Total/overall, section/component scores, percentile vs recent cohort, validity dates, verification number (TRF/registration number), and sometimes subscores or proficiency levels (e.g., CEFR for English, deciles for UCAT, bands for IELTS/PTE/CELPIP, scaled + subscores for GRE).

| Report Component | Example for TEAS 7 | How Institutions/Employers Use It |
|------------------|---------------------|-------------------------------------|
| **Total / Overall** | 0-100% per section + composite (e.g., 7.0, 650, AIR 5000, 300/400) | Primary filter for merit lists, cutoffs, scholarships — overall threshold |
| **Section / Component** | Per-skill/seat (e.g., Reading 7.5, Quant 48, Paper 1 90/180) | Used for sectional cutoffs — **failing a section disqualifies even if overall high** (common in India, UK, Canada, Australia: CAT sectional 80, UCAT SJT, IELTS no less than 6.0, PTE no less than 58, CELPIP CLB) |
| **Subscores / Profiles** | Diagnostic breakdown (e.g., CEFR B2, UCAT decile, CFA topic band) | Often NOT used for admissions; diagnostic for your preparation only — do not over-index |
| **Percentile / Rank** | vs recent cohort (nationally representative vs test-taker pool) | Context for "how competitive is 1200 vs 1350?" — test-taker percentile (vs actual takers) is what competitive programmes see |

**Percentiles — two contexts you must distinguish for TEAS 7:**
- **Nationally representative percentile:** vs all eligible candidates (including non-takers) — higher numbers (e.g., 1200 SAT ~ 75th nationally)
- **Test-taker pool percentile:** vs actual TEAS 7 takers — lower numbers, more relevant for competitive programmes (e.g., 1200 SAT ~ 65th among takers) — this is what admissions file readers see in the US undergraduate context; other contexts similar

**Reporting timeline & validity for TEAS 7:**
- Digital/CBT: often **2-5 days** (e.g., TOEFL iBT 4-13 days, IELTS computer 3-5 days, PTE 48h, Duolingo 48h, GMAT Focus 3-5 days, GRE 8-10 days)
- Paper: **2-3 weeks** (e.g., IELTS paper 13 days, UPSC prelims ~10 days)
- At-home/Online: similar to digital
- Validity: **2 years** for English proficiency (for visas — UKVI/Australia Home Affairs/IRCC enforce 2-year-at-entry) or **2-5 years** for admissions/licensure (e.g., GRE/GMAT/MCAT 3-5 years, JEE Advanced rank only that year) — verify your programme's "valid at course start" definition, not just test date

**Score verification for TEAS 7:** TRF/registration/AR number verifiable online (e.g., IELTS TRF verification at ieltsverification.org, ETS/GMAC at ets.org/mba.com verification, NTA via DigiLocker, UPSC marksheet).

### What Is 'Good' for TEAS 7? — Program-Specific, Not Universal

There is no universal "good" for TEAS 7. There is only "competitive for YOUR targets." A 1200 SAT is competitive for a regional public and uncompetitive for an Ivy; a 7.0 IELTS is competitive for Canada CLB 9 and uncompetitive for Oxford. Same for every TEAS 7.

1. List your 8-12 targets (reach: admit rate <15% or AIR <1000; match: 15-40% or AIR 1000-10000; safety: >40% or qualifying + margin). For TEAS 7, targets are programmes, institutions, licensing boards, or immigration streams.

For each target, find its published **middle 50% (25th-75th)** or **median/AIR/cutoff** or **previous-year cut-off** or **previous-year departmental cutoff** for TEAS 7 — search "[Exact Institution + Exact Programme] + TEAS 7 + Common Data Set / admission statistics / previous-year cut-off / departmental marks / AIR / NTA score / UCAT decile" for the most recent completed cycle (not 3 years ago).
3. Goal for TEAS 7:
   - **Safety / licensure qualifying:** at/above **75th percentile** (or pass threshold + margin, e.g., +5-10 points/bands, or +0.5 band for IELTS, +100 rank buffer for JEE/NEET)
   - **Match:** at/above **75th** for overall competitiveness
   - **Reach:** at/above **median (50th)** is minimum viable; below 25th is uncompetitive

### Superscore / ScoreSelect / Score Choice / Revaluation for TEAS 7

Policy varies more by **institution/counselling body** than by test:

| Policy | What It Means for TEAS 7 | What You Should Send for TEAS 7 |
|--------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| **Superscore** | Best section scores across dates recombined into new total/average (e.g., SAT/ACT superscore, GRE informal) | All dates where you have a best section — institution calculates |
| **Highest Single Sitting** | Best overall in one sitting only — sections not mixed | Single best date only for TEAS 7 |
| **All Scores Required** | Institution sees every sitting (e.g., Georgetown/Yale for SAT/ACT, some medical schools) | All dates (no choice) — retake only if upward trend likely |
| **Test-Blind / Test-Optional** | Score not used or optional (e.g., UC system test-blind, many post-COVID flexible) | Optional submit — submit if at/above median; withhold if below 25th where non-test profile compensates |
| **Revaluation / One Skill Retake / Enquiry / EOR** | TEAS 7-specific: ATI may offer remarking (e.g., IELTS EOR, UPSC RTI copy), One Skill Retake (IELTS OSR within 60 days), MyBest (TOEFL) — verify if YOUR institution/counselling (JoSAA/MCC/CAP/UCA) accepts retooled scores | Check per counselling body — e.g., IELTS OSR accepted by 1,200+ orgs as of 2024 but not Oxbridge/medicine; TOEFL MyBest by 90% US but not some UK |

**General strategy for TEAS 7:**
- For **superscore institutions** -> send all dates where you have a best section — they calculate the best composite
- For **highest single sitting** -> send single best TEAS 7 date only
- For **test-optional/test-blind** -> submit if at/above median for that institution; withhold if below 25th where essays/GPA/work/portfolio compensates
- For **immigration (CELPIP/IELTS/PTE/CELPIP)**: IRCC/Australia Home Affairs/UKVI do NOT superscore — threshold must be met in one sitting

### Retake Decision Framework for TEAS 7 — Is Another Sitting Worth It?

#### Expected Gain on Retake for TEAS 7 (Illustrative, varies by preparation quality)

| Preparation Level for TEAS 7 | Typical Gain | With Domain/Gating Fix (highest ROI) |
|-------------------------------|--------------|----------------------------------------|
| **Light (10-20h, informal)** | +2 to +5% (or +0.5 band / +3-5 scaled points / +500-1000 rank improvement rank-dependent) | +5-8% on focused section |
| **Serious (40+ hours, targeted on weakest 2 domains, official materials)** | +5 to +10% (or +0.5-1.0 band / +10-20 scaled points / +2000-5000 rank) | +10-15% if gating or access to hard difficulty/sectional cutoff fixed |
| **Gating Fix (unlocking hard Section 2, fixing time management, overcoming word-limit penalties)** | +8 to +15% on total — single largest ROI for TEAS 7 | Frontier gain |

**For TEAS 7 with hard cutoffs:** Retake ROI is binary — 0.5 band / 10 scaled points below = zero for automatic merit (e.g., UKVI, CLB, scholarship) while 0.5/10 above = threshold met + funding.

#### Decision Tree for TEAS 7

```
Is score below 25th percentile (or below sectional cutoff) for ALL targets/counselling cutoffs?
  -> YES -> Retake + broaden institution/counselling list to include matches where you are already 75th+
Is one section >=1.3 SD below the others (e.g., Quant 8.0 but Writing 6.0 for IELTS)?
  -> YES -> Section-specific preparation (not full retake prep) -> Retake — highest ROI per hour for TEAS 7
Is score in 25th-75th for top-choice target?
  -> Do you have 6-8 weeks before deadline/counselling with 12h/week available?
     -> YES -> Targeted preparation on highest-weight weak domain for TEAS 7 -> Retake
     -> NO  -> Do not retake; submit and strengthen other components (essays, work, portfolio) — marginal gain not worth opportunity cost
Is score >75th for top-choice target?
  -> Only retake for specific scholarship/fellowship cutoff (often +0.5 band / +10-20 scaled points = USD 10k-30k/year) or if rank can improve into higher scholarship band
Undecided for TEAS 7?
  -> Take 1 official full practice test under full conditions including timing/breaks: if practice >5% above real score (or +0.5 band), retake; if within 3%, do not — variance
```

**Retake constraints for TEAS 7:**
- Waiting period: 3 days for TOEFL/IELTS/PTE/DET, 21 days for GRE, 16 days for GMAT Focus, 1-7 days for many Indian CBTs (check ATI)
- Attempt limits: 5 per 12 months for GMAT/GRE, 3 per year for LSAT, 2 consecutive years for JEE Advanced, unlimited for many
- Delivery: Can switch paper <-> computer between sittings (where offered) — choose delivery that suits your practice

**Cost of retake for TEAS 7:** Full fee again (or OSR at 65% for IELTS) + opportunity cost of 40-60 preparation hours — compare to funding gain.

FULL ARTICLE:

The KCSE (Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education) is a high-stakes gate within School-Leaving — administered by KNEC + KUCCPS and taken by tens to hundreds of thousands annually to determine admission, progression, or licensure. Unlike low-stakes internal exams, KCSE is **externally validated, scaled, and normed**: your score is compared against a national/international cohort, not just your class. This guide explains the live 2024-2025 format with verified timing, question distribution, ID rules, and centre logistics so you arrive with zero surprises.

---

### What Is the KCSE and Who Needs It?

**Core purpose:** Measure the competencies your target institution or regulator has defined as prerequisite for success — whether academic readiness, professional judgment, or language proficiency for study/work/migration.

**Take KCSE if:**
- Your 8-12 specific target institutions, employers, or immigration streams **explicitly list KCSE** as accepted/required (check each programme page: "Accepted tests: KCSE" — not just a generic testing page)
- You need a portable, externally verified score for merit scholarships, visas, or multi-country applications
- Your diagnostic percentile on KCSE is higher than on alternatives

**You may not need KCSE if:**
- Your targets are **test-optional/test-blind** and your non-test profile (GPA, work, portfolio) is already at 75th percentile
- An alternative test is accepted equally and your alternative diagnostic is higher
- You qualify for an exemption (e.g., English-medium degree waiver for English tests, prior licensure)

**Decision before booking:** Screenshot the exact line from your target's admissions/immigration page: "KCSE — minimum ...". Generic "English test required" is not enough — confirm KCSE by name.

### Format at a Glance (2024-2025 Verified)

| Component | Duration / Questions | What Is Tested | Delivery Detail |
|-----------|---------------------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Overall** | 7-9 subjects (3 compulsory + 4-6 optional), exams Oct-Nov, 2-3h per paper | Domain-specific content per School-Leaving | A(12) to E(1), mean grade, C+ (46 pts) = university qualification |
| **Primary Section(s)** | See official bulletin for KCSE (distribution varies by form/session) | Applied reasoning and knowledge synthesis | Check official specifications for section-level adaptivity vs linear |
| **Secondary / Integrated** | Varies by paper/elective/specialism | Communication, professional judgment, data interpretation | Integrated tasks where applicable |

**Key 2024-2025 changes for KCSE:**
- Digital/CBT is now primary in most regions — verify paper vs computer vs at-home for your centre (some regions phased out paper)
- Scoring scale stable (A(12) to E(1), mean grade, C+ (46 pts) = university qualification) but percentile tables shift annually — use 2024 table for interpretation
- Calculator and aid policies updated — see "Tools" below
- Validity 2-3 years for language/immigration, 3-5 years for admissions/licensure — confirm with regulator

**Tools (allowed aids) for KCSE:**
- Calculator: Check official calculator policy (on-screen for many CBTs; physical where allowed must be approved model — e.g., no CAS, no QWERTY, no paper tape)
- Reference: Formula sheet for some (e.g., SAT, FE) vs no sheet for others (e.g., GATE, JEE Advanced, CFA) — know before you memorise
- Rough work: Whiteboard/erasable sheet for at-home/CBT (1 sheet in sheet protector) vs scratch paper at centre

### Section-by-Section Deep Dive for KCSE

#### Primary Domain (Largest Weight — Where Rank Is Decided)

**Why it matters:** The primary domain contributes 35-50% of your total/score. For KCSE, this is where 80th vs 90th percentile is decided. Example patterns:
- Knowledge-recall items (20-30%): Direct definition or formula — free if memorised, lost if not
- Comprehension items (30-40%): Apply concept to passage/data — requires reading, not recall
- Analysis items (20-30%): Synthesize 2-3 concepts — the differentiator; requires multi-step reasoning
- Evaluation items (10%): Judge sufficiency or best argument — hardest; requires logic

**Hard-item preview for KCSE:**
- Item with 3-4 concept integration (e.g., thermodynamics + equilibrium + kinetics)
- Item requiring graph extraction in 15 seconds + calculation
- Item with trap operator: NOT, EXCEPT, LEAST, CANNOT, MUST vs COULD

**Strategy:** Master the 3 most frequent sub-types in this domain first — they yield 60% of points.

#### Secondary Domain(s)

**Data/Analytical:** Ratios, conditional probability, distribution, correlation — restrict denominator to condition; watch units; correlation with observational data is not causation (only experiments with controls support causation).

**Communication:** Synthesis across sources — identify pivot words (however, although, because, therefore), predict answer before options, match functional equivalence not synonym.

**Integrated/Case:** Evolving item types in licensure (NCLEX NGN, UCAT SJT, CFA ethics) — practice with official sample items, not third-party.

### Registration: Step-by-Step for KCSE (2024-2025)

#### 1. Create Official Account
Use KNEC + KUCCPS's portal. Enter legal name exactly as on government ID/passport (including middle name, hyphen, diacritics). This account is permanent — use a personal email you will retain.

#### 2. Verify Eligibility Before Paying
- Education: degree level, board, percentage/percentile, caregory certificate format (central vs state)
- Age: lower and upper bounds, and date-of-reference
- Attempts: max per year/lifetime (e.g., JEE Advanced 2 consecutive, GMAT 5 per 12 months)
- Documents: photo (80% face), signature, thumb, ID number, self-declaration where required

#### 3. Choose Delivery, Date, and City
- **Test dates:** Book 6-10 weeks ahead for preferred dates; peak (Sep-Nov, Jan-Mar, May for Indian exams) fills 2 months early. International centres fill 2-3 months ahead.
- **Cities:** Choose 3-8 preferences; allotment by computer — you may not get first choice in peak.
- **At-home (where offered):** Verify technical (OS, browser, lockdown, camera, mic) and environment (private room, door closed, clear desk, whiteboard only) **2 weeks before** — do the official system check.

#### 4. Provide Information and Score Recipients
- High school/university codes, photo upload, intended programmes, background questionnaire (optional but used for search/scholarships)
- Score recipients: 4-5 free if listed within 1 month of test (check free TRF/report policy for KCSE); additional ~USD/GBP 20-35 each.

#### 5. Pay and Confirm
- Fee varies by country/category — check KNEC + KUCCPS for your country (fees adjust 2x/year) — screenshot confirmation.
- Confirmation email + reference number saved — needed for admit card and TRF verification.

**Fee reduction:** Many KCSE administrations offer need-based waivers (e.g., ACT/SAT/GRE/GMAT fee waivers for low-income, GATE/CEED SC/ST waiver) — apply 4-6 weeks before intended test.

#### 6. Download Admit / Confirm Centre
Admit / city slip 1-2 weeks before → check reporting time (often 30 min before gate closes). Visit centre if unfamiliar — reduce test-day anxiety.

---

### Scoring for KCSE: How Your A(12) to E(1), mean grade, C+ (46 pts) = university qualification Is Calculated

**Scale:** A(12) to E(1), mean grade, C+ (46 pts) = university qualification — scaled, not raw. Two candidates with same raw can have different scaled due to equating (form difficulty) or adaptivity weighting.

**Percentiles:** Annual, based on recent cohort (e.g., 2023-2024 test-taker pool). Your test-taker percentile (vs actual takers) is what competitive programmes see; nationally representative (vs all eligible) is higher.

**Cutoffs/Criteria:**
- Fixed benchmark (e.g., 75 to pass for CPA, C for A-Level, C+ for KCSE, 50th percentile for NEET qualifying)
- Rank-based (e.g., JEE Advanced, GATE, CAT, UCAT deciles, JAMB departmental) — rank, not marks, determines seat
- Sectional + overall (e.g., CAT 80 sectional, UCAT SJT Band 1-2) — failing a section = no offer even if overall high

**Reporting timeline:** Digital/CBT often 2-5 days; paper 2-3 weeks; validity 2 years (language for visas) or 3-5 years (admissions) — check your programme's "valid at course start" definition.

**Score verification:** TRF/registration number verifiable online (e.g., IELTS TRF verification, ETS/GMAC score verification).

---

### Test Day: What to Bring, What to Expect at the Centre

**Required:** Admit + same ID as registration (passport for most international; government/school ID where allowed — UKVI/CELPIP/IELTS for UKVI always passport) + TRN/reference + transparent water bottle.

**Prohibited:** Phones (off and in locker — touching during break = disqualified), watches (including analogue), notes, food (except at designated break), unauthorised calculators.

**Centre experience (typical 08:00-15:00 for paper, shorter for CBT):**
07:30 Check-in (ID, photo, biometrics — finger/palm, bag in locker)
08:30 Tutorial + Section 1(s) — no pause within timed sections
11:00 Break (10-30 min, designated area only)
11:30 Section 2(s)
13:00 Survey + unofficial scores if provided
**CBT nuance:** Headphones provided, highlight/flag/eliminator on screen, 2-min review at end (no extra transfer like paper Listening).

### Official Practice Resources — The Only Authentic Predictor

**Free (start here, on KNEC + KUCCPS portal):**
- Official practice test (1-2 full tests free) — diagnostic gold
- Sample questions with answers and band descriptors / scoring guides
- Preparation portal/app with timed practice

**Paid (use after free — in order of authenticity):**
- Official guide (3-6 authentic past tests) — e.g., Cambridge IELTS 10-19 (10 tests), Official GMAT Guide (900 Qs), AAMC FLs (4), LSAC PrepTests (70+)
- Official online practice (computer simulation with timer)
- Official coaching/live online (mock Speaking / interview where applicable)

**Sequence:** Diagnostic (full, timed, 2.5-3h) → score per section using official table → identify weakest 2 sections → targeted practice (hardest items first) → Test 2 → Test 3 the week before.

**Do NOT:** Use non-official practice for score prediction — difficulty is inflated/deflated and adaptive algorithm not replicated.

### International Candidate Notes for KCSE

- **Centre choice:** Competing networks (e.g., British Council vs IDP for IELTS, NTA vs TCS iON for Indian exams) — same test, choose closer/cheaper/earlier date.
- **Retake:** Waiting period varies (3 days TOEFL/IELTS, 21 days GRE, 16 days GMAT Focus, 1 day for many Indian CBTs) — unlimited for most but cost; some adjust superscore/OSR (e.g., IELTS One Skill Retake within 60 days — check if YOUR institution accepts OSR; many UK/Australia do, some Oxbridge/US do not).
- **Visa vs admission:** English tests for admission vs for visa (UKVI, Australia Home Affairs, IRCC) may differ — a standard TRF may be invalid for visa. Verify with immigration authority, not just university.

### Frequently Asked Questions for KCSE

**Q: Can I take KCSE on paper vs computer?**
A: Many KCSE administrations are now digital/CBT primary; paper remains in some regions or for accommodations. At-home exists for select tests. Verify with official bulletin for your country/centre — do not assume.

**Q: How many times can I take it?**
A: Attempt limits vary (e.g., 2 attempts/consecutive years for JEE Advanced, 5 per 12 months for GMAT/GRE, unlimited for IELTS/TOEFL/PTE but cost). Most candidates take 1-3 times; schools/regulators see only scores you elect to send but some require all.

**Q: What is a 'good' score for KCSE?**
A: No universal threshold. It is 'at/above 75th percentile for your safety/match targets, at/above median for reach'. Search "[Institution/Course] + KCSE + Common Data Set / admission statistics / previous-year cutoff" for the most recent cycle — that is your target.

**Q: When should I start preparing for KCSE?**
A: Ideal 8-12 weeks for focused preparation; minimum 4-6 weeks intensive. Diagnostic first — do not build a plan without baseline + timing data.

**Q: Does KCSE have negative marking?**
A: Check marking scheme per question type: MCQ -1/3 to -1, TITA/NAT 0, multiple-correct partial credit — changes guessing strategy.

3. **Official practice tests are the only authentic predictor** — prioritize them over any third-party.
4. **Register early** — preferred dates/cities fill 6-10 weeks ahead; international 2-3 months.
5. **8-12 weeks focused preparation** with official materials and an error log is the proven path.

### Phase 0: Diagnostic — Week -1 (Non-Negotiable Before Any Plan)

Take one full official practice test for KCSE under **real conditions**: timed, same delivery (paper/computer/centre/online), correct tools (calculator policy per KCSE), real breaks, no pauses, no lookups.

**Record on one page:**

| Metric | Your Score | Target | Gap | Notes |
|--------|------------|--------|-----|-------|
| Total / Composite / Overall | | | | Percentile? |
| Section 1 | | | | Weakest domain — priority 1 |
| Section 2 | | | | Weakest domain — priority 2 |
| Section 3/4 if applicable | | | | |
| Timing left / rushed / guessed | | | | Pacing fix needed? |
| Delivery comfort (paper vs computer) | | | | Decide before Week 1 |

**Error log (spreadsheet — mandatory from Day 1):** Date | Section | Q# | Domain | Format (MCQ/TITA/NAT/WR) | Error Type (Content / Careless / Timing / Strategy) | Root Cause | Fix Action | Retest Date

**Categorise every miss for KCSE:**
- Content: Did not know formula / definition / rule
- Careless: Misread operator (NOT/EXCEPT), unit, selected wrong variable, darkening error
- Timing: Spent >2x average and still wrong → skip candidate
- Strategy: Did not use allowed aid (Desmos/calculator/highlight/whiteboard) or misapplied

**Decision point after diagnostic for KCSE:**
- Within 10% of target → Weeks 1-2 = advanced tactics + pacing refinement (not content)
- 20-30% below → Weeks 1-2 = content mastery on weakest 3 domains (official question bank, easiest → hardest)
- >30% below → Extend foundation to 6 weeks before heavy simulation; add 2 weeks to calendar

For KCSE, the diagnostic also reveals delivery fit — do all subsequent practice in the delivery you will sit.

---

### Weeks 1-2: Foundation — Close Content Gaps (The Highest-ROI Weeks)

**Goal:** 80%+ on official question banks for weakest 3 domains/subjects for KCSE.

| Activity | Hours | Method for KCSE |
|----------|-------|---------------------|
| Weak Domain Practice | 6 | Official question bank: easiest -> hardest, untimed then timed; tag each with domain |
| Diagnostic Review | 3 | Deep-dive every wrong answer: write why correct is correct + why your choice is wrong |
| Content Review | 2 | Official syllabus/bulletin for KCSE — not coaching summaries or social media |
| Mini-Timed Sets | 1 | 10-15 questions mixed domains, 70% of full time — build discrimination |

**Domain priority for KCSE (School-Leaving):**
- If verbal/reading/listening is weak: argument structure, inference, T/F/NG vs Y/N/NG distinction, vocabulary in context, note-taking for audio-once
- If quantitative is weak: arithmetic foundations (percent, ratio, averages, time-speed, time-work), algebra, data interpretation, geometry/trigonometry (formula-dependent)
- If writing/integrated is weak: task achievement (overview, position, bullet coverage), cohesion (paragraphing, linking, reference), citation of evidence vs opinion
- If data/science/professional judgment is weak: graph extraction in 15 seconds, variable/control identification, ethics application

**Vocabulary / Formula / Mechanism system (where applicable for KCSE):** Start spaced repetition Day 1 (Anki/Quizlet) — 20 new/day + daily review. For KCSE this may be words, formulas, organic mechanisms, or statutes depending on domain; the system matters more than the list. 5 min review at morning/evening.

**Deliverable end of Week 2:** Complete official practice sets for weakest 3 domains at 80%+. Re-take diagnostic Section 1(s) — target 75%+. If not, repeat Week 2 — do not proceed; foundation is the base for KCSE.
